findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md §4 and AGENTS.md §3 codemaps missing docs/postmortems/ and docs/templates/
findings.detail: Both directories exist on disk but were absent from the repo tree in ARCHITECTURE.md §4 (Codemap) and AGENTS.md §3 (Repo structure). Added to both.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md §1 NON_GOALS.md anchor wrong (#no-gos vs #no-gos-never-not-not-yet)
findings.detail: Line 21 cited `NON_GOALS.md#no-gos` but the actual section header is `## No-Gos (never, not "not yet")`, which GitHub renders as `#no-gos-never-not-not-yet`. Corrected.

findings.title: CHANGELOG.md ### Decisions subsection not in Keep a Changelog's 6 allowed categories
findings.detail: Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 allows only: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security. Renamed `### Decisions` to `### Notes` in the initial scaffold section.

findings.title: ADR-0001/-0003/-0010 cite truncated anchor #5-architectural-invariants
findings.detail: Correct anchor is #5-architectural-invariants-explicit-absences. Cannot fix: ADR-0001, ADR-0003, and ADR-0010 all have status: accepted. Editing accepted ADRs is blocked by the pre-commit hook (.husky/pre-commit) and the Never rule in AGENTS.md §7.

findings.title: ADR-0006 status 'superseded by ADR-0011' not in canonical 4-value set
findings.detail: MADR does not restrict status values to 4 options; 'superseded by ADR-0011' is a valid MADR pattern carrying the superseder reference inline. Not a defect.

findings.title: 6 spec files use non-canonical status values (skeleton, living, incomplete)
findings.detail: Values skeleton, living, incomplete are defined in the Factory spec lifecycle and are intentional. The 4-value ADR set (proposed/accepted/rejected/superseded) applies only to ADRs in docs/decisions/, not to the 17 spec files.

findings.title: KPI.md and RUNBOOK.md have status: skeleton but contain substantial content
findings.detail: Status skeleton means 'populated when first production data/incident is captured' (per frontmatter comment). Having substantial placeholder/template content is expected at this stage; the status reflects data readiness, not content volume.
